{"path":"effect_gouraud_shaded_cube_anthropic-claude-sonnet-5_01.html","edit_description":"
Create a complete, self-contained single HTML file implementing a realtime Gouraud-shaded rotating cube using only Canvas 2D (no WebGL, no external libraries). Requirements:

1. Full HTML document with inline <style> and inline <script> — no external files/CDNs.
2. Dark page background, a centered <canvas> (e.g. 800x600, resizable via devicePixelRatio for sharpness), and a small on-screen HUD/overlay (top-left, semi-transparent panel) showing:
   - Current FPS (updated ~every 250-500ms, smoothed)
   - Wireframe: ON/OFF state
   - Paused: yes/no
   - Instructions: "W = toggle wireframe, P = pause/resume"
3. Minimal 3D pipeline implemented from scratch in plain JS (no libraries):
   - Cube defined as 8 vertices (Vec3) centered at origin.
   - 3x3 rotation matrices around X, Y, and Z axes (or a combined rotation matrix), composed each frame from time-varying angles so the cube continuously rotates on multiple axes.
   - A simple perspective projection function (camera at some distance on +Z looking at origin, focal length / fov based projection) mapping camera-space 3D points to 2D screen coordinates, also keeping the camera-space Z for depth sorting/culling.
   - Backface culling: compute each face's normal (from two edge vectors of the transformed face, in camera space) and the vector from camera to the face; cull faces whose normal points away from the viewer (dot product test), i.e. only draw front-facing triangles.
4. The cube has 6 faces (quads); split each quad into 2 triangles (12 triangles total), each with its own base color (distinct color per cube face is fine, e.g. red, green, blue, yellow, magenta, cyan) used as the material color for lighting.
5. Lighting: a point light (or directional-ish point light) whose position moves over time (e.g. orbits around the cube in a circle using sin/cos of time), computed in world/camera space consistently with the cube transform. Per-vertex Lambertian lighting: for each triangle vertex, compute a vertex normal (face normal is fine, reused per vertex of that triangle) and the light direction from vertex to light position (normalized), then lit color = baseColor * (ambient + diffuse * max(0, dot(normal, lightDir))). Clamp channel values to [0,255].
6. Gouraud shading rasterization: after backface culling and lighting, project the 3 triangle vertices to screen space with their computed lit RGB colors, then rasterize the filled triangle interpolating color per-pixel (or per-scanline) across the triangle using barycentric coordinates (implement a standard scanline/barycentric triangle rasterizer directly on ImageData or via manual scanline fill — must show visible color interpolation across each triangle face, not a flat single color per face). Depth-sort the visible triangles (painter's algorithm using average/max camera-space Z, back-to-front) before drawing, since there's no z-buffer requirement stated but z-ordering must look correct for a convex cube.
7. Wireframe toggle (key "W" or "w"): when enabled, draw only the triangle/edge outlines (stroke) instead of (or in addition to, your choice, but faces should not obscure the concept — simplest: draw wireframe edges only, no fill) filled Gouraud shading; toggling should be instantaneous and re-affect subsequent frames.
8. Pause toggle (key "P" or "p"): stops updating rotation angles and light position (freeze the scene) but the render loop / FPS counter can keep running or also freeze — either way clearly show "Paused: yes" in the HUD and no further motion happens until unpaused.
9. Use requestAnimationFrame for the render loop with delta-time based animation (not fixed per-frame increments) so speed is consistent regardless of frame rate.
10. Keep everything in one file: no external scripts, styles, fonts, or images. No frameworks. No WebGL context — only canvas.getContext('2d').
11. Code should be clean, well-commented, organized into logical sections/functions (vector math helpers, matrix/rotation helpers, projection, lighting, rasterizer, main loop, input handling).
12. Make sure canvas sizing accounts for devicePixelRatio for crisp rendering, and handle window resize gracefully (re-center cube).

Produce the entire file content now.
"}
